audit: VERTEX Kattis candidate original-statement evidence ledger — pass 3
method: Original contest statement sources were inspected for title/problem identity, narrative, input/output, and constraints. Statement identity does not independently verify live Kattis URL or long-scenario qualification.

records.title: Coast Length
records.statementTitle: KTH Challenge 2011, Problem E — Coast Length
records.identity: title and problem ID coast explicitly match
records.observed: The municipality of Soteholm models sea-level scenarios on a grid and asks for the length of the coastline, excluding lakes and inland water not connected to map edges.
records.excerpt: The residents of Soteholm value their coast highly and therefore want to maximize its total length.
records.inputOutput: Input: N×M binary land/water map. Output: total sea-coast length.
records.constraints: N and M each at most 1,000; grid dimensions and connectivity rules are specified.
records.scenarioNotes: Distinctive climate/municipal planning context and explicit topological distinction between sea and lakes, but the algorithmic task remains a single grid flood-fill. Long-scenario qualification not approved.

records.title: Nikola
records.statementTitle: Croatian Open Competition in Informatics 2007/2008, Croatian Regionals — Task NIKOLA
records.identity: title Nikola and game description match; candidate source year is corroborated as 2007/2008
records.observed: Nikola moves along numbered squares, with jump length depending on the previous jump and direction; entering a square incurs a fee and the goal is minimum total cost.
records.excerpt: Against his own will, Nikola has become the main character in a game. The game is played on a row of N squares, numbered 1 to N.
records.inputOutput: Input: N and entry fees for each square. Output: minimum total cost to reach square N.
records.constraints: 2 ≤ N ≤ 1,000; each entry fee is positive and less than 500.
records.scenarioNotes: Narrative is only a light game wrapper around a constrained-jump shortest-path/DP problem; likely not a long scenario. Formal quality gate remains pending.

records.title: Canonical Coin Systems
records.statementTitle: North America Qualifier 2017, Problem C — Canonical Coin Systems
records.identity: title and contest problem C match; Kattis slug canonical corroborated by candidate source metadata
records.observed: The statement defines coin denominations and asks whether greedy change-making always yields an optimal number of coins, using cashier/change-making as context.
records.excerpt: A coin system S is a finite (nonempty) set of distinct positive integers corresponding to coin values, also called denominations, in a real or imagined monetary system.
records.inputOutput: Input: coin denominations with required conditions. Output: whether the system is canonical, according to the statement's specified contract.
records.constraints: The original statement provides denomination count and maximum denomination limits; preserve exact values when enriching the canonical record.
records.scenarioNotes: Real-world cashier/change-making context, but the scenario is a standard coin-system property test and likely too compact for long-scenario classification.
